To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dual CFT of RS model with bulk gauge fields has a large-N expansion and that this CFT loop expansion is dual to the full gauge field propagator with external points on the brane.

(i) the dual CFT has an UV cut-off, (ii) in the absence of a bare kinetic term for a gauge field coupled to the CTF global current, the kinetic term is ``induced'', and (iii) loop corrections to the coupling constant of a gauge field in the CFT is sensitive to strong dynamics of the theory.

the limit of the RS model with small brane-localized gauge kinetic term on the brane is dual to no (or small bare) kinetic term for a gauge field coupled to a CFT global current in the dual CTF, and loop corrections in the RS model are dual to subleading effects in a large N expansion in the dual CDT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the dual CFT for the RS model with gauge field in the bulk?
the study of the dual CFT of the RS model in the limit of no or small kinetic term for bulk fields on the RS side.
the study of the duality between the RS model with gauge field in the bulk and a CFT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RS model with gauge field in the bulk is (at least) a dual of an N = 1 CFT with a bare gauge kinetic term.
the RS model with gauge field in the bulk is equivalent to a strongly coupled 4D CFT in which global symmteries are gauged, with the CFT loop effects playing an important role in this equivalence.

the weakly coupled RS model with gauge field in the bulk is equivalent to a strongly coupled 4D CFT with an ultraviolet cut-off in the limit that the CFT is weakly coupled and the brane-localized gauge kinetic term is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CFT dual to RS model with gauge field in the bulk is a 4D CFT which is strongly coupled, with an UV cut off, and whose global symmetries are gauged; the CFT is not necessarily a large-N limit of a 4D gauge theory, and its strong dynamics are crucial for a full understanding of the RS/CFT duality.

the RS model with bulk gauge fields and no brane-localized gauge kinetic term is dual to the CFT in which the bare gauge coupling is absent and the gauge field is coupled to CFT global current, and the gauge coupling is determined by CFT loops and is sensitive to strong dynamics of the theory.

the RS gauge model with a non-zero brane-localized gauge kinetic term on the Planck (IR) brane is dual to a strongly coupled 4D CFT with a large bare kinetic term for a gauge field which is gauged and coupled to the CTF currents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual CFT has to be understood as a strongly-coupled CFT with an explicit UV cut-off, in which the CFT global symmetries are gauged.

, for a complete understanding (and a possible proof) of the proposed dualities, one needs to go beyond the weakly coupled (perturbative) description of the gauge field in the RS model and also to go beyond the leading order in a large-N limit of the dual CFT.

, in the limit in which the gauge field on the Planck-brane has vanishing kinetic term (and hence no gauge bosons on the brane), the RS model with bulk gauge fields is dual to a strongly-coupled CFT with an UV cutoff, in which the global symmetries are gauged and in which there is a large-N limit.
